model_organism.citation: Grone et al. 2016 - Epilepsy, Behavioral Abnormalities, and Physiological Comorbidities in Syntaxin-Binding Protein 1 (STXBP1) Mutant Zebrafish (PMID: 26963117)
phenotypes: CRISPR/Cas9 loss-of-function mutants of stxbp1a and stxbp1b
Homozygous stxbp1a mutants: profound lack of movement, low brain electrical activity, low heart rate, decreased glucose and mitochondrial metabolism, early fatality
Homozygous stxbp1b mutants: spontaneous electrographic seizures and reduced locomotor response to dark-flash stimulus
stxbp1b mutants had normal metabolism, heart rate, survival and baseline locomotion
model_organism.lethality: stxbp1a homozygotes: early larval fatality; stxbp1b homozygotes: viable

biological.citation: Reduced dynamin-1 levels in neurons lacking MUNC18-1 (PMID: 36245272)
biological.summary: In Stxbp1 null neurons, syntaxin-1 is reduced by 70%, dynamin-1 protein is reduced at least as much, and Dnm1 transcripts are reduced by 50%. Other endocytic proteins are also reduced. Co-IP showed that dynamin-1 and MUNC18-1 do not bind directly. The reduction was not seen in SNAP25 null or Munc13-1/2 double-null neurons, and dynamin-1 overexpression did not rescue viability. This suggests MUNC18-1 directly or indirectly controls expression of presynaptic genes.

biological.citation: Homozygous STXBP1 variant causes encephalopathy and gain-of-function in synaptic transmission (PMID: 31855252)
biological.summary: In Munc18-1 null mouse neurons, the homozygous L446F variant was less destabilized than heterozygous disease mutants. It caused a 2-fold increase in evoked synaptic transmission, reduced paired-pulse plasticity, and slower recovery after stimulus trains. Spontaneous release, readily releasable pool size and morphology were normal. This is a gain-of-function mechanism in release probability.

biological.citation: Targeted stabilization of Munc18-1 function via pharmacological chaperones (PMID: 33332765)
biological.summary: Munc18-1 is essential for neurotransmitter release. Missense mutations cause aggregation and co-aggregation of wild-type protein, which lowers functional Munc18-1 below hemizygous levels. Two structure-based pharmacological chaperones bound wild-type and mutant Munc18-1 and reverted aggregation and neuronal dysfunction in vitro and in vivo.

biological.citation: Epilepsy, Behavioral Abnormalities, and Physiological Comorbidities in Syntaxin-Binding Protein 1 (STXBP1) Mutant Zebrafish (PMID: 26963117)
biological.summary: Zebrafish stxbp1a and stxbp1b are highly conserved and prominently expressed in larval brain. CRISPR stxbp1a homozygous mutants showed a profound lack of movement, low brain activity, low heart rate, decreased glucose and mitochondrial metabolism, and early death. stxbp1b mutants had spontaneous electrographic seizures and a reduced dark-flash response, with normal metabolism, heart rate and survival.

biological.citation: Virtual Screening and Zebrafish Phenotype-Based Evaluation Argues Against Repurposing 4-Phenylbutyrate for STXBP1-Related Disorders (PMID: 42268630)
biological.summary: stxbp1a mutant zebrafish larvae showed a locomotion deficit at 5 dpf. 4-PBA and 16 AI-identified analogs failed to rescue it, and 4-PBA did not reduce ictal-like events in stxbp1b mutants. This argues against repurposing 4-PBA, despite its rescue of C. elegans models.

biological.citation: Phenotypic assessment of Stxbp1 haploinsufficiency reveals neurological disabilities in serotoninergic system (PMID: 41263692)
biological.summary: C. elegans UNC-18 (STXBP1) deficiency caused progressive dendritic atrophy of serotonergic neurons. Stxbp1 haploinsufficient mice had fewer serotonergic neurons, decreased 5-HT, and compensatory upregulation of serotonin receptors. Serotonergic-neuron-specific haploinsufficiency recapitulated a subset of the neurological phenotypes.

biological.citation: Human brain slice culture model of STXBP1 encephalopathy reveals disruption of neuronal network activity and changes in gene expression (PMID: 42214744)
biological.summary: shRNA knockdown of STXBP1 in foetal human organotypic cortical cultures (15-18 PCW) reduced the amplitude and synchronicity of subplate network activity. It dysregulated genes involved in synaptogenesis, ion transport and extracellular matrix organisation. Neurites were shortened and the axon-guidance receptor EPHA4 accumulated at growth cones.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - α-Synuclein pathology in Drosophila melanogaster is exacerbated by haploinsufficiency of Rop : Connecting STXBP1 encephalopathy with α-synucleinopathies
biological.summary: Drosophila Rop (the STXBP1 homolog) null homozygotes are embryonic lethal. Heterozygotes survive with about 20% lower protein. Rop haploinsufficiency increased insoluble α-synuclein, reduced dopamine neuron number, impaired motor function and worsened eye degeneration. Trehalose reduced insoluble α-synuclein and restored locomotion, supporting an STXBP1–α-synuclein interaction.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 3136: Humanized STXBP1 animal models as a precision medicine approach to detecting pathogenicity in clinical variants
biological.summary: Human STXBP1 replaced C. elegans unc-18 and rescued function: 100% by electrophysiology and in thrashing, and 50% in chemotaxis. Variants R292H, R406H and R388X showed functional defects. R388X, a two-thirds truncation, acted dominant-negatively in the heterozygote, about 3-fold more severe than a heterozygous full knockout.

biological.citation: CASK, APBA1, and STXBP1 collaborate during insulin secretion (PMID: 33159991)
biological.summary: Co-IP and LC-MS showed that CASK, APBA1 (X11α) and STXBP1 form a tripartite complex during insulin secretion. CASK enhances the APBA1–STXBP1 interaction and their trafficking to the plasma membrane. High fatty acid exposure decreased their expression, and Cask overexpression rescued lipotoxicity-induced secretion defects.
